content: It is important to attend all scheduled medical and laboratory appointments. If you miss a dose of this medication, take it as soon as you remember. However, if it is close to the time of your next dose or late in the evening, skip the missed dose and resume your regular dosing schedule. Do not double the dose to catch up. Store this medication at room temperature, away from light and moisture. Avoid storing it in the bathroom. Do not flush medications down the toilet or pour them into a drain unless specifically instructed to do so. Properly discard this product when it is expired or no longer needed. This information was last updated in May 2024. Please note that this is a summary and does not include all possible details about this product. It does not guarantee that the product is safe, effective, or appropriate for you. This information is not a substitute for personalized medical advice. Always consult your healthcare professional for complete information about this product and your specific health needs. Before taking this medication, inform your doctor or pharmacist if you are allergic to it, to other sympathomimetic amines (such as pseudoephedrine, amphetamines, or appetite suppressants like diethylpropion), or if you have any other allergies. This product may contain inactive ingredients that could cause allergic reactions or other issues. This medication may cause dizziness, blurred vision, or, in rare cases, drowsiness. Alcohol or marijuana (cannabis) can exacerbate these effects. Avoid driving, operating machinery, or performing tasks that require alertness or clear vision until you can do so safely. Refrain from consuming alcoholic beverages. If you have diabetes, monitor your blood sugar levels regularly as directed and share the results with your doctor. If you are using orally dissolving tablets, be aware that they may contain aspartame. This medication should not be used during pregnancy, as it may harm an unborn baby. Additionally, it may pass into breast milk and could have undesirable effects on a nursing infant. Breastfeeding is not recommended while using this medication. Drug interactions may alter how your medications work or increase the risk of serious side effects. This document does not include all possible drug interactions. Keep a list of all the products you use, including prescription and non-prescription drugs and herbal products, and share it with your doctor and pharmacist. This medication should not be used with certain other drugs due to the risk of severe interactions. For example, taking MAO inhibitors (such as isocarboxazid, linezolid, methylene blue, phenelzine, or tranylcypromine) with this medication may result in a serious, potentially fatal interaction. Avoid taking MAO inhibitors during treatment with this medication and for two weeks before starting it. Caffeine can also intensify the side effects of this medication. This medication may interfere with certain medical or laboratory tests, such as brain scans for Parkinson’s disease, potentially causing false test results. Inform your healthcare provider and laboratory personnel that you are using this medication. In the event of an overdose, if someone has serious symptoms such as passing out or difficulty breathing, call 911 immediately. Otherwise, contact a poison control center right away. U.S. residents can call 1-800-222-1222, and Canadian residents can call 1-844-764-7669. Appetite suppressants should not be used as a substitute for a proper diet. Do not share this medication with others. Always follow your healthcare provider’s instructions and keep all medical and laboratory appointments.
